verdict.rationale: Open WebUI's docs say it is self-hosted and 'built to run entirely offline', with Ollama and OpenAI-compatible APIs for local models and an air-gapped deployment option. A connect-a-model page in the related Computer docs names Ollama, vLLM and LM Studio as OpenAI-compatible providers added via a custom Base URL. llama.cpp is never named, and no hands-on report confirms a fully local, cloud-free setup. missing for 10: explicit llama.cpp support documentation, core-product (not Computer-ecosystem) docs naming vLLM/LM Studio, independent or hands-on corroboration of fully offline local-model operation.

support.subject: As a privacy-first user, I can run the assistant entirely on local models — Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, or vLLM — with no cloud model dependency

citations.quote: self-hosted AI platform that's extensible, feature-rich, user-friendly, and built to run entirely offline
With support for Ollama and OpenAI-compatible APIs, it gives you a powerful, provider-agnostic interface for both local and cloud-based models.
anything that speaks the OpenAI API (Ollama, OpenRouter, vLLM, LM Studio, Groq, ...) is added as provider OpenAI with a custom Base URL.
Air-Gapped: Complete network isolation for environments with the strictest security requirements.
